decisions.mark: locates the macro's definition in include/mbedtls/private_access.h
states that by default the macro RENAMES the member to private_<member>, and that defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS makes it expand to the member name unchanged

explains that the two branches give different consumers different views — code that defines MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names while an ordinary consumer of the public headers sees the renamed ones
concludes that this enforces API opacity at COMPILE time by breaking the member name, rather than by hiding the struct layout — the fields remain visible and sized
conveys that the macro is applied at a scale of many hundreds of sites, overwhelmingly in the public headers rather than in library implementation
states that library-internal code turns the opt-out ON in a shared header, so every library translation unit sees plain member names
identifies that some example programs ALSO define the opt-out for themselves, deliberately reaching past the public API they otherwise demonstrate
